text:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] PagerDuty PDR-12345 -> 5xx spike detected on /v1/generate (inference-api). 30s sustained, multiple customer errors. Severity: SEV3. Auto-escalation in 5m if unacknowledged. Logs: https://pd.redwood/pdr/PDR-12345.

oncall-bot: Details: region=eu-west, endpoint=inference-api, error=504/502 burst, traffic increase ~2.1x. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/5xx-spike (recommended steps).

maria: saw this while grabbing a gate latte. i'm actually on PTO today but my badge still green in PD. primary was expected to be me this shift — I left a note in rotation that i'd be offline from 00:00-08:00Z. :(  @aaron are you the scheduled secondary?

aaron: yep i'm the scheduled secondary but i'm in transit right now (delayed train). i can take primary if someone can shadow for the first 20–30m. i have phone but limited laptop time. i'll ack the PD if nobody else can.

jin: i can shadow remotely for now, ping on the bridge. can someone paste the quick mitigation checklist? don't want to dig through the long runbook mid-pager.

sam: quick checklist — 1) confirm PD ack + bridge, 2) check model-worker CPU/mem & pod restart count, 3) switch to fallback model variant if available, 4) scale worker group, 5) clear prefix cache if stuck. i'll help with scaling.

maria: thanks. tagging the runbook snippet I left in rotation: `encode:priority=scale->fallback->restart`. if fallback exists, prefer it for external customer traffic and let batch jobs finish on degraded variant.

aaron: okay taking it. i'm accepting PDR-12345 now. setting myself primary in rotation and notifying SRE head. creating bridge.

deploy-bot: Bridge created by aaron: https://meet.redwood/bridge/PDR-12345 (pin this). Token for bridge posted to PD incident.

oncall-bot: PD ack detected: user=aaron. Auto-escalation cancelled.

aaron: quick telemetry — CPU on model-worker-x is at 95% for the last 3m, pod restarts = 2 in 10m, queue depth spike on request-queue. suspect KV cache thrash + a few heavy prompts. attaching recent log tail:

aaron: ```
[2026-03-15T02:12:14Z] INFO request id=bb8c client=acme corp seq=1 latency=124ms
[2026-03-15T02:12:17Z] ERROR model-worker-x pid=2213 ERR OOM while allocating KV cache
[2026-03-15T02:12:18Z] WARN request id=bb9d dropped -> 502 upstream error
[2026-03-15T02:12:20Z] ERROR bulk retry limit reached for queue request-queue
```

jin: plan: 1) scale model-worker-x replica count 4 -> 8, 2) rotate traffic to fallback `model-x-1-quant` for public routes, 3) restart the two flapping pods after new pods are ready to avoid double-dip. sam can you run the scale? i'll monitor metrics and check logs for OOM stack traces.

sam: running scale now. command: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy/model-worker-x --replicas=8` — kicking off. i'll post updates.

sam: (reaction :gear:) scale started — new pods scheduling. expected ready in ~90s.

deploy-bot: Scaling event: model-worker-x replicas 4 -> 8 requested by sam. Pod templates unchanged. Rolling update in progress.

aaron: while we wait, switch the public route to fallback to avoid more customer 5xx. steps: update routing-config in console -> route-inference /v1/generate -> service=fallback-model-x. someone with console rights do that?

jin: i can flip it in console, give me the green. doing it now.

jin: updated route to fallback-model-x (traffic ~30% -> fallback for external public API). monitoring latency and error rate.

aaron: nice. error rate dropping from 18% -> 6% in last 45s. keep an eye on throttles.

sam: new pods are ready. `kubectl get pods -l app=model-worker-x` shows all `Running` and `Ready=true`. I'm going to cordon and restart the two old pods flagged for restarts to clear any stuck caches: `kubectl delete pod <pod-old-1> <pod-old-2>`

sam: deleted old pods; new ones picked up. health checks passing.

aaron: after restarts + routing change, 5xx rate stabilised to 1.3% — back within SLA for hosted tier customers. i'll keep primary for the next 2 hours to observe. moving to manual override in PD so no auto-handoff. :heavy_check_mark:

maria: huge thank you to @aaron @jin @sam. i'm going to add a note to rotation: if primary is marked PTO, ensure secondary has explicit ack or we risk ghost-rotation. also adding link to quick mitigation snippet to the rotation doc.

oncall-bot: Incident PDR-12345 -> status: mitigated by aaron. duration ~8m. summary: scale + fallback + pod restarts. Actions opened: follow-up ticket TKT-9876 to investigate OOM root cause and add autoscale buffer for peak windows.

aaron: filing a short post-incident note in the incident channel and assigning TKT-9876 to infra for deeper memory profiling. I'll hand back the primary in rotation once I'm off the bridge.

jin: leaving as shadow for 30m, will escalate if trend returns.

maria: noted. happy to pick up retrospective when I'm back. enjoy the bridge team. :coffee:

oncall-bot: Reminder: if error rate rises again, PD auto-escalate in 30m. Keep an eye on canary and error budget.

deploy-bot: Bridge closed (no active participants) — summary saved to PD incident.

aaron: closing thread here. log snippet and timeline saved to PD + runbooks updated with a short `how-to` for ghost-rotation checks.

maria: thanks all, filing a quick rotation doc update now. :wave:
